templates.pattern: An object of mass [M] kg moves in a horizontal circle of radius [R] m at a constant speed of [V] m/s. Calculate the centripetal acceleration of the object in m/s².
templates.explanation:
Centripetal acceleration = v² ÷ r
= [V]² ÷ [R]
= [V*V] ÷ [R]
= [RESULT] m/s²

Centripetal acceleration always points toward the centre of the circle. It is not a new force — it is the resultant of existing forces acting on the object.

templates.pattern: An object of mass [M] kg moves in a circle of radius [R] m at a constant speed of [V] m/s. Calculate the centripetal force acting on the object in newtons.
templates.explanation:
Centripetal force = mv² ÷ r
= [M] × [V]² ÷ [R]
= [M] × [V*V] ÷ [R]
= [RESULT] N

Centripetal force is always directed toward the centre of the circle. For a car on a bend this is friction. For a planet in orbit this is gravity.

templates.pattern: A ball is launched horizontally from the top of a cliff of height [H] m. Calculate the time taken for the ball to reach the ground in seconds. (g = 10 m/s², ignore air resistance)
templates.explanation:
Vertical motion only determines time of flight.
Using s = ½gt² with s = H and u = 0:
H = 0.5 × 10 × t²
t = √(2H ÷ g)
= √(2 × [H] ÷ 10)
= √[2*H/10]
= [RESULT] s

Horizontal velocity does not affect the time of flight. Both components of motion are completely independent.

templates.pattern: A ball is launched horizontally at [U] m/s from the top of a cliff of height [H] m. Calculate the horizontal distance travelled by the ball before it hits the ground in metres. (g = 10 m/s², ignore air resistance)
templates.explanation:
Time of flight t = √(2H ÷ g) = √(2 × [H] ÷ 10) s
Horizontal range = U × t
= [U] × √(2 × [H] ÷ 10)
= [RESULT] m

Horizontal velocity remains constant throughout the flight because there is no horizontal force acting on the ball.

templates.pattern: A rocket ejects gas at an exhaust velocity of [VE] m/s. The rocket ejects [DM] kg of gas every second. Calculate the thrust force produced by the rocket in newtons.
templates.explanation:
Thrust force = exhaust velocity × mass flow rate
= [VE] × [DM]
= [RESULT] N

This is an application of Newton's Third Law. The rocket pushes gas backward and the gas pushes the rocket forward with an equal and opposite force.

templates.pattern: An object of mass [M] kg falls through a fluid and reaches terminal velocity. Calculate the drag force acting on the object at terminal velocity in newtons. (g = 10 m/s²)
templates.explanation:
At terminal velocity the resultant force is zero.
Drag force = Weight = mg
= [M] × 10
= [RESULT] N

Terminal velocity is reached when drag force equals weight. At this point acceleration is zero and velocity is constant.

templates.pattern: An object moves in a circle of radius [R] m at a linear speed of [V] m/s. Calculate the angular velocity of the object in rad/s.
templates.explanation:
Angular velocity ω = v ÷ r
= [V] ÷ [R]
= [RESULT] rad/s

Angular velocity measures how fast the object rotates. One full revolution = 2π radians. The unit is radians per second (rad/s).

templates.pattern: An object moves in a circle of radius [R] m at a linear speed of [V] m/s. Calculate the period of one complete revolution in seconds.
templates.explanation:
Period T = circumference ÷ speed
= 2πr ÷ v
= 2 × 3.14159 × [R] ÷ [V]
= [RESULT] s

The period is the time for one complete revolution. It is related to frequency by T = 1/f.

templates.pattern: A [M1] kg object moving at [U] m/s collides with a stationary [M2] kg object. After the collision the [M2] kg object moves at [V2] m/s. Calculate the velocity of the [M1] kg object after the collision in m/s.
templates.explanation:
Using conservation of momentum:
m₁u = m₁v₁ + m₂v₂
v₁ = (m₁u − m₂v₂) ÷ m₁
= ([M1] × [U] − [M2] × [V2]) ÷ [M1]
= ([M1*U] − [M2*V2]) ÷ [M1]
= [RESULT] m/s

Total momentum before = total momentum after. This is always true in a closed system.

templates.pattern: A [M] kg object moving at [V] m/s is brought to rest over a distance of [S] m by a constant retarding force. Calculate the magnitude of the retarding force in newtons.
templates.explanation:
Using the work-energy theorem:
Work done by retarding force = loss in kinetic energy
F × s = ½mv²
F = mv² ÷ 2s
= [M] × [V]² ÷ (2 × [S])
= [M] × [V*V] ÷ (2 × [S])
= [RESULT] N

The retarding force converts all kinetic energy to other forms such as heat through friction.
